text:
Tye Kartye went undrafted, played his way out of the AHL in Seattle, and is now a regular part of the Rangers' conversation: Sports Illustrated has written twice this month about his production, and Blue Line Station thinks New York should sign him long term before the price climbs.

The role is the story. He's playing 16:56 a night, up from 11:58 last season, he's getting power-play time for the first time, and he's at 14 points in 23 games, nearly double last year's rate. His own chances have more than doubled too, to 1.01 expected goals per 60 minutes.

His seven goals sit right on 6.6 expected, so the scoring is earned. If anything the line has been unlucky: the Rangers have scored 5.7 fewer goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice, and his trio with J.T. Miller and Pavel Dorofeyev has taken 64% of the expected goals while being outscored.

He's also thrown 60 hits. What to watch: his minutes have climbed past 19 lately, and he's reached that on a line that should start seeing the puck go in.
